# 1 Chronicles Chapter 15 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 378v–379r

---

**1** David built several buildings for himself in the City of David. He also prepared a special place for the ark of God and set up a tent for it.

**2** Then David declared, "Only the Levites may carry the ark of God, because the LORD chose them for this sacred task — to carry the ark of the LORD and to serve him forever."

**3** David then assembled all Israel in Jerusalem to bring the ark of the LORD to the place he had prepared for it. **4** He gathered the descendants of Aaron and the Levites:

**5** from the clan of Kohath — Uriel the leader, with 120 relatives; **6** from the clan of Merari — Asaiah the leader, with 220 relatives; **7** from the clan of Gershom — Joel the leader, with 130 relatives; **8** from the clan of Elizaphan — Shemaiah the leader, with 200 relatives; **9** from the clan of Hebron — Eliel the leader, with 80 relatives; **10** from the clan of Uzziel — Amminadab the leader, with 112 relatives.

**11** David summoned the priests Zadok and Abiathar, along with the Levite leaders Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab. **12** He told them, "You are the heads of the Levite families. Purify yourselves — you and all your fellow Levites — so you can bring the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel, to the place I have set aside for it. **13** The first time, we did not follow the proper procedure, and the LORD our God burst out in anger against us. We failed to seek him in the way he requires."

**14** So the priests and Levites purified themselves to bring up the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel. **15** Then the Levites carried the ark of God on their shoulders, using the carrying poles — exactly as Moses had commanded in accordance with the LORD's word.

**16** David instructed the Levite leaders to appoint musicians from among their relatives — singers accompanied by instruments: lyres, harps, and cymbals — to play joyful music at full volume.

**17** The Levites appointed Heman son of Joel; from his relatives, Asaph son of Berechiah; and from the Merarites, Ethan son of Kushaiah.

**18** Assisting them in the second rank were: Zechariah, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, and the gatekeepers Obed-edom and Jeiel.

**19** The lead musicians — Heman, Asaph, and Ethan — played bronze cymbals. **20** Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah played lyres tuned to a high pitch. **21** Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah led the music with harps tuned to a low pitch.

**22** Chenaniah, chief of the Levites, was the music director — he took charge because of his expertise. **23** Berechiah and Elkanah served as guards for the ark. **24** The priests Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer blew trumpets in front of the ark of God. Obed-edom and Jehiah also served as guards.

**25** So David, the elders of Israel, and the commanders of thousands went with great joy to bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD up from the house of Obed-edom. **26** Because God helped the Levites who were carrying the ark of the LORD's covenant, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams in gratitude.

**27** David was wearing a robe of fine linen, as were all the Levites carrying the ark, the singers, and Chenaniah the music director. David also wore a priestly linen ephod. **28** All Israel brought the ark of the LORD's covenant up to Jerusalem with joyful shouts, to the blasting of rams' horns, the sounding of trumpets and cymbals, and the music of lyres and harps.

**29** But as the ark of the LORD's covenant entered the City of David, Michal daughter of Saul was watching from an upstairs window. When she saw King David leaping and dancing with abandon, she was filled with contempt for him.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 2 — "Only the Levites":** This sentence changes everything. David has learned from the disaster of chapter 13. The cart — borrowed from Philistine practice — is gone. In its place: human shoulders, Levitical poles, Torah obedience. The Chronicler's point is not that God is arbitrary but that God's holiness has a shape, and that shape is revealed in Scripture.

**Verse 13 — "We failed to seek him in the way he requires":** This is one of the most theologically dense sentences in Chronicles. David does not blame Uzzah, does not blame God, and does not blame the ark. He blames the method — "we did not seek him *ka-mishpat*," according to the prescribed way. Sincere worship offered in the wrong form is still wrong. The Chronicler insists that devotion and order are not opposites.

**Verse 26 — "Because God helped the Levites":** A remarkable theological statement. When the Levites carried the ark, God "helped" them — the same ark that killed Uzzah when carried on a cart. The difference is not physical (the ark weighs the same either way) but covenantal. Obedience creates the conditions for divine cooperation.

**Verse 29 — Michal's contempt:** The daughter of Saul, watching from a window, despises the dancing king. Windows in the ancient world are observation points for those who do not participate. Michal stands at the boundary between Saul's dynasty and David's — watching, judging, excluded. The Chronicler says nothing more about her; her contempt is its own verdict.

*— PNEUMA*
